accepted.name: gsod2000_normalized_dates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS stn,
  wban AS wban,
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS year_int,
  SAFE_CAST(mo AS INT64) AS month_int,
  SAFE_CAST(da AS INT64) AS day_int,
  DATE(SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(mo AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(da AS INT64)) AS obs_date,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS temp_f,
  count_temp AS count_temp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(dewp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS dewp_f,
  count_dewp AS count_dewp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(slp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS slp_mb,
  count_slp AS count_slp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(stp, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS stp_mb,
  count_stp AS count_stp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(visib, 999.9), 999.9) AS visib_mi,
  count_visib AS count_visib,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '999.9') AS FLOAT64) AS wdsp_kt,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(count_wdsp, '9999') AS INT64) AS count_wdsp,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(mxpsd, '999.9') AS FLOAT64) AS mxpsd_kt,
  NULLIF(gust, 999.9) AS gust_kt,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(max, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS max_f,
  flag_max AS flag_max,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(min, 9999.9), 9999.0) AS min_f,
  flag_min AS flag_min,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(prcp, 99.99), 99.99) AS prcp_in,
  flag_prcp AS flag_prcp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(sndp, 999.9), 999.9) AS sndp_in,
  fog AS fog_flag,
  rain_drizzle AS rain_drizzle_flag,
  snow_ice_pellets AS snow_ice_pellets_flag,
  hail AS hail_flag,
  thunder AS thunder_flag,
  tornado_funnel_cloud AS tornado_funnel_cloud_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2000`

semantic_filters.none: No question-specific filters; sentinel values converted to NULL

accepted.description: Normalize gsod2000 daily rows to a proper DATE, cast numeric sentinels to NULLs and pass through station identifiers and key measures. Use this as a clean day-level weather fact table for joins and aggregations. | Use for: time series of temperature/precipitation at station or aggregated by region; join station metadata to get lat/lon and compute spatial aggregates; compute monthly/annual summaries, anomalies, and missingness

accepted.name: stations_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf AS usaf,
  wban AS wban,
  name AS station_name,
  country AS country,
  state AS state,
  call AS call_sign,
  lat AS latitude,
  lon AS longitude,
  NULLIF(elev, '') AS elevation_raw,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', begin) AS begin_date,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', `end`) AS end_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`

semantic_filters.none: No additional filters; parse begin/end when available

accepted.description: Cleaned stations dimension with canonical keys (usaf/wban), numeric lat/lon and parsed begin/end as DATE. Use for joining station metadata to observations. | Use for: lookup station coordinates for mapping weather observations; filter stations by country/state or active periods; join with normalized gsod2000 to enrich observations with station metadata

accepted.name: gsod2000_with_station_lookup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.* EXCEPT(stn, wban),
  g.stn AS stn_key,
  g.wban AS wban_key,
  s.usaf AS station_usaf,
  s.wban AS station_wban,
  s.station_name,
  s.country,
  s.state AS station_state,
  s.latitude AS station_latitude,
  s.longitude AS station_longitude,
  s.begin_date AS station_begin_date,
  s.end_date AS station_end_date
FROM gsod2000_normalized_dates AS g
LEFT JOIN stations_core AS s
  ON (g.stn = s.usaf) OR (g.wban = s.wban)

semantic_filters.none: Left join preserves observations without station metadata; no question-specific filters

accepted.description: Left-join normalized gsod daily observations to station metadata using both usaf/stn and wban keys. Preserve both join keys and station attributes; useful for spatial or regional aggregations. Implemented as LEFT JOINs to avoid dropping observations missing station metadata. | Use for: compute regional aggregates (by country/state) of weather metrics; map observations to coordinates for spatial analysis; identify station active ranges for time windowed analyses

accepted.name: storms_1963_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  episode_id AS episode_id,
  event_id AS event_id,
  location_index AS location_index,
  state AS state,
  state_fips_code AS state_fips_code,
  event_type AS event_type,
  cz_type AS cz_type,
  cz_fips_code AS cz_fips_code,
  cz_name AS cz_name,
  wfo AS wfo,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATETIME('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', CAST(event_begin_time AS STRING)) AS event_begin_dt,
  SAFE.PARSE_DATETIME('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', CAST(event_end_time AS STRING)) AS event_end_dt,
  COALESCE(injuries_direct, 0) AS injuries_direct,
  COALESCE(injuries_indirect, 0) AS injuries_indirect,
  COALESCE(deaths_direct, 0) AS deaths_direct,
  COALESCE(deaths_indirect, 0) AS deaths_indirect,
  COALESCE(damage_property, 0) AS damage_property,
  COALESCE(damage_crops, 0) AS damage_crops,
  source AS source,
  magnitude AS magnitude,
  magnitude_type AS magnitude_type,
  tor_f_scale AS tor_f_scale,
  tor_length AS tor_length,
  tor_width AS tor_width,
  reference_location AS reference_location,
  event_latitude AS event_latitude,
  event_longitude AS event_longitude,
  event_point AS event_point
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_1963`

semantic_filters.none: No question-specific filters; parses datetimes safely and defaults numeric nulls to 0 for counts/damages

accepted.description: Clean storms_1963 location rows, expose parsed event times, numeric measures, and geographic point. Use for event-level analyses and spatial joins to point reports. | Use for: count storms by type or state; join with wind_reports by spatial/temporal proximity; aggregate casualties/damages by area or event type

accepted.name: wind_reports_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  timestamp AS timestamp_utc,
  SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%E6S', CAST(timestamp AS STRING)) AS ts_parsed,
  time AS time_utc_hour,
  speed AS speed_mph,
  location AS location_name,
  county AS county,
  state AS state,
  latitude AS latitude,
  longitude AS longitude,
  comments AS comments,
  report_point AS report_point
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.wind_reports`

semantic_filters.none: No filters; preserves all reports for flexible temporal or spatial windows downstream

accepted.description: Normalized wind reports: parse timestamp, keep speed and coordinates, and expose report_point geography for spatial joins. | Use for: identify highest wind reports in a period or region; spatially join wind reports to storm events or counties; time-series of extreme wind occurrences

accepted.name: wind_reports_speed_ranked
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.*,
  DATE(ts_parsed) AS report_date,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(ts_parsed) ORDER BY speed_mph DESC) AS rank_by_day,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state, DATE(ts_parsed) ORDER BY speed_mph DESC) AS rank_by_state_day,
  MAX(speed_mph) OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(ts_parsed)) AS max_speed_day,
  MAX(speed_mph) OVER (PARTITION BY state, DATE(ts_parsed)) AS max_speed_state_day
FROM wind_reports_core AS w

semantic_filters.none: No question-specific literal thresholds; ranks exposed so callers can filter rank<=K

accepted.description: Assign rank and running maximum per day and per state for wind report speeds. Useful for top-k wind reports queries or selecting daily maxima. | Use for: top-k wind gust reports nationally or by state/day; identify daily maxima and compare across states

accepted.name: storms_events_daily_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(event_begin_dt) AS event_date,
  state AS state,
  COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS distinct_events,
  SUM(injuries_direct) AS total_injuries_direct,
  SUM(injuries_indirect) AS total_injuries_indirect,
  SUM(deaths_direct) AS total_deaths_direct,
  SUM(deaths_indirect) AS total_deaths_indirect,
  SUM(damage_property) AS total_damage_property,
  SUM(damage_crops) AS total_damage_crops
FROM storms_1963_core
GROUP BY event_date, state

semantic_filters.none: No fixed temporal or state filters; aggregates available for any date/state

accepted.description: Aggregate storms_1963 to one row per event_date and state with summed casualties and damages. Useful for statewide daily impact summaries and trend analyses. | Use for: time series of casualties/damages by state or nationwide; correlate storm impacts with weather observations or population exposure
